arguments.title: Mutation-graded test suite for interval.mjs boundaries
arguments.spec:
# Spec: mutation-graded test suite for interval.mjs

- `src/interval.mjs` is frozen and correct. The suite must never modify `src/`, `mutants/`, `test/mutation.test.js`, `test/frozen-digests.json`, `package.json`, or `scripts/`.
- The suite lives only under `test/agent/**` as `*.test.js` files using `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, plus entries in `tests/manifest.json`.
- The suite must never import `node:fs`, `node:child_process`, `node:vm`, `node:module`, or `node:worker_threads`; never reference a `mutants/` path; never assert on `Function.toString()`; and never use real timers or the real clock.
- Every mutant id listed in `tests/manifest.json`'s `killed` array must be genuinely killed: the full suite passes against the correct `src/` and fails against that mutant's shadowed copy.
- Kill mutant m1 by proving mergeIntervals([]) returns [] without throwing (the empty-collection guard).
- Kill mutant m6 by proving widest() on a single-interval list returns that interval, not null (the singleton case).
- Kill mutants m4 and m5 by proving contains() treats both endpoints as inside exactly at the boundary.
- Kill mutants m2 and m3 by proving mergeIntervals treats touching intervals (a gap of exactly one) as mergeable, and keeps the farthest end when one interval is swallowed by another.
- Kill mutant m7 by proving clampToBounds returns the point unchanged exactly at the top of the range, only clamping strictly above it.
- Set `"complete": true` in `tests/manifest.json` only once every one of the seven mutants is killed, then rerun `npm test` to confirm the frozen verifier passes end-to-end.

tasks.prompt:
Constraints (apply to every card in this project): never edit `src/`, `mutants/`, `test/mutation.test.js`, `test/frozen-digests.json`, `package.json`, or `scripts/` — their digests are pinned and checked on every `npm test` run. Add a manifest entry only once every assertion needed to kill that mutant is written and passing for real by running `npm test` — never fabricate output. Keep `"complete": false` until the close-out card.

Your slice: mergeIntervals' empty-collection guard (`intervals.length === 0` weakened to `< 0`, which never fires) (mutant m1). Diff it yourself: `diff src/interval.mjs mutants/m1/interval.mjs`. These are boundary-input mutants (not history/sequence ones) — a single well-chosen call at the exact edge usually distinguishes correct from broken, but check both endpoints/directions so you don't half-cover it. Write `test/agent/empty-boundary.test.js` (plain ESM, `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, importing from `../../src/interval.mjs`). Then add to `tests/manifest.json`'s `killed` array: {"id": "m1", "why": "the empty-array guard must fire or mergeIntervals breaks on empty input"}. Run `npm test` for real and read its actual output — it must show the baseline test passing and the mutant-kill test(s) for m1 passing (the mutant genuinely fails). Report the real tail of that output; never fabricate it.
